questions.q: The keyboard shortcut to increase the indent of a paragraph in MS Word is:
questions.solution: Ctrl+M increases indent, Ctrl+Shift+M decreases it. (Tab indents only at the start of a paragraph/list item; Ctrl+I is italic.)
questions.shortcut: M = More indent; add Shift = less.

questions.q: Which key **edits the active cell** in Excel?
questions.solution: **F2** puts the cell in edit mode — the keyboard version of a double-click.

questions.q: In MS Word, Ctrl+J applies which alignment to the selected paragraph?
questions.solution: Ctrl+J justifies text so both margins are straight. Left is Ctrl+L, centre is Ctrl+E and right is Ctrl+R.

questions.q: **PDF** (the extension .pdf) stands for —
questions.solution: **Portable Document Format** — a fixed-layout document that looks identical on every device, opened in readers like Adobe Reader or a browser.

questions.q:
Select the option that can substitute the given group of words.

The act of killing one's own brother
questions.solution: Frater = brother → **fratricide**. *Patricide* kills the father, *regicide* the king, *genocide* a whole community — all -cide family-mates separated by the relation root.
questions.shortcut: Family root decides the relation: frater = brother.

questions.q:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.

The officer said to the clerk, "File these papers immediately."
options: The officer ordered the clerk to file those papers immediately.
The officer ordered the clerk to file these papers immediately.
The officer ordered the clerk filing those papers immediately.
The officer ordered to the clerk to file those papers immediately.
questions.solution: **ordered the clerk to file those papers immediately** — the order takes to + V1 and these shifts to those. 'To file these papers' leaves the demonstrative unshifted; 'ordered the clerk filing' breaks the infinitive; 'ordered to the clerk' inserts a to that ordered never takes.

questions.q:
Select the word which is most opposite in meaning to the given word.

VIRTUE
questions.solution: *Virtue* = moral goodness → its standard opposite is **vice** (moral fault). 'Value' drifts to worth, and the v-initial 'virtuosity/vigour' are shape decoys.
questions.shortcut: Kill the v-initial decoys; pick the genuine moral opposite.

questions.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number (4).
questions.solution: The fixed phrase is **make room for** = clear space for someone: the traders now 'make room for her boards'. *Do room* and *take room* are not English; *give room* would need a different sense ('give way to'). Collocation decides.
questions.shortcut: room → make (make room for). Learn the pair, not the logic.
questions.passage: Every Sunday, Farida sets up chessboards in the park behind the market and teaches whoever stops to watch. What began as a pastime has become a small (1) ______: forty children from the nearby lanes attend her free class. She insists that chess does not (2) ______ talent alone; it rewards habit. 'A (3) ______ player who studies one game a day will soon beat a player who plays ten games carelessly,' she says. The market traders, who once asked her to move away, now (4) ______ room for her boards every Sunday morning.

questions.q:
Consider the statements:
1. Arya Samaj launched shuddhi (reconversion) ceremonies.
2. The Singh Sabha (1873) worked for Sikh revival.
3. The Mahad Satyagraha (1927) was led by Periyar.
Which are correct?
questions.solution: Statements 1 and 2 are right. The **Mahad Satyagraha was led by B.R. Ambedkar**, not Periyar (whose movement is the Self-Respect Movement).

questions.q: **Calcination** involves heating —
questions.solution: **Calcination = carbonate ore, limited air** (CO₂ is driven off); **roasting = sulphide ore, excess air** (SO₂ escapes). Both leave the oxide.

questions.q:
Consider the statements:
1. National Science Day marks the Raman effect (1928).
2. Army Day is observed on 15 January.
3. Hindi Diwas marks the adoption of Hindi as official language in 1949.
Which are correct?
questions.solution: All three are settled: 28 February (Raman 1928), 15 January (Cariappa 1949), 14 September (1949 resolution).

questions.q: **14 major commercial banks** were nationalised in —
questions.solution: On **19 July 1969** fourteen big private banks were nationalised; **six** more followed in **1980**, deepening credit reach.

questions.q: Two numbers are in the ratio 2 : 3 and their LCM is 48. The sum of the numbers is:
questions.solution:
Let the numbers be $2k$ and $3k$ (co-prime parts).
LCM $= 6k = 48$ ⇒ $k = 8$.
Numbers: 16 and 24 ⇒ sum $= 40$.
questions.shortcut: LCM of a 2:3 pair is 6k = 48 ⇒ k = 8 ⇒ 16 + 24 = 40.

questions.q: What is the area (in square units) of the triangle formed by the line $3x+4y=24$ and the coordinate axes?
questions.solution:
$x$-intercept: put $y=0$ → $x=8$. $y$-intercept: put $x=0$ → $y=6$.

Area $=\frac12\times8\times6=24$ square units.
questions.pattern: area of triangle made by a line with axes

questions.q: Which of the following fractions is the smallest?
questions.solution: Gaps from 1: $\frac{4}{17} \approx 0.235$, $\frac{3}{14} \approx 0.214$, $\frac{4}{19} \approx 0.211$, $\frac{2}{11} \approx 0.182$. The biggest gap belongs to $\frac{13}{17}$, so it is the smallest.
questions.shortcut: Complement method: biggest shortfall from 1 = smallest fraction.

questions.q:
Production of cars (in thousands) by four companies:

| Year | P | Q | R | S |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2019 | 120 | 90 | 150 | 80 |
| 2020 | 135 | 110 | 145 | 95 |
| 2021 | 150 | 105 | 160 | 100 |
| 2022 | 140 | 125 | 170 | 110 |
| 2023 | 165 | 130 | 175 | 120 |

Which company showed the highest percentage increase in production from 2019 to 2023?
questions.shortcut: P has the biggest absolute rise (45) but the biggest base too; S doubles half-way (40 on 80).

questions.q:
Select the number that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series.

**2, 3, 5, 8, 13, 21, ?**
questions.solution: Each term = sum of the previous two: 8 + 13 = 21, so next = 13 + 21 = **34**.

questions.q: A square sheet is folded in half from left to right, and one hole is punched exactly on the folded edge (the crease), halfway up. How many holes does the opened sheet have?
questions.solution: A punch on a crease makes no separate copy: the mirror image of the hole across the fold line falls on the same spot, so the two plies open as just **1** hole, on the crease.
questions.shortcut: Holes = sum of the layers under each punch.

questions.q:
In each triangle the corners are (left, right, top) and a number sits in the centre:

**(2, 3, 4) → 20**

**(1, 5, 3) → 18**

**(4, 2, 5) → ?**
questions.solution: Product of corners fails (24 ≠ 20), sum fails (9). Rule: centre = (left + right) × top: (2 + 3) × 4 = 20 ✓, (1 + 5) × 3 = 18 ✓. So (4 + 2) × 5 = **30**. (40 is the product of all three corners.)
questions.shortcut: Centre just below the corner product → try (x + y) × z.

questions.q:
A survey of **100 people** on how they get news — Newspaper (N), TV (T) and Radio (R) — gave these region counts:

- Only N: 20 · Only T: 25 · Only R: 5
- N and T only: 15 · T and R only: 6 · N and R only: 4
- All three: 10 · None of the three: 15

How many people use **exactly one** source?
questions.solution: Exactly one = only N + only T + only R = 20 + 25 + 5 = **50**. 65 wrongly adds the 15 who use none; 35 is the at-least-two count.
